```
     3→import (
     4→	"context"
     5→	"net/http"
     6→
     7→	"github.com/sentioxyz/changelogue/internal/models"
     8→)
     9→
    10→// TodosStore defines the data access interface for TODO operations.
    11→type TodosStore interface {
    12→	ListTodos(ctx context.Context, status string, page, perPage int) ([]models.Todo, int, error)
    13→	GetTodo(ctx context.Context, id string) (*models.Todo, error)
    14→	AcknowledgeTodo(ctx context.Context, id string) error
    15→	ResolveTodo(ctx context.Context, id string) error
    16→}
    17→
    18→// TodosHandler handles HTTP requests for release TODOs.
    19→type TodosHandler struct {
    20→	store     TodosStore
    21→	publicURL string
    22→}
    23→
    24→// NewTodosHandler creates a new TodosHandler.
    25→func NewTodosHandler(store TodosStore, publicURL string) *TodosHandler {
    26→	return &TodosHandler{store: store, publicURL: publicURL}
    27→}
    28→
    29→// List returns a paginated list of TODOs, optionally filtered by status.
    30→func (h *TodosHandler) List(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    31→	page, perPage := ParsePagination(r)
    32→	status := r.URL.Query().Get("status")
    33→
    34→	todos, total, err := h.store.ListTodos(r.Context(), status, page, perPage)
    35→	if err != nil {
    36→		RespondError(w, r, http.StatusInternalServerError, "internal_error", err.Error())
    37→		return
    38→	}
    39→	if todos == nil {
    40→		todos = []models.Todo{}
    41→	}
    42→	RespondList(w, r, http.StatusOK, todos, page, perPage, total)
    43→}
    44→
    45→// Get returns a single TODO by ID.
    46→func (h *TodosHandler) Get(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    47→	id := r.PathValue("id")
    48→	todo, err := h.store.GetTodo(r.Context(), id)
    49→	if err != nil {
    50→		RespondError(w, r, http.StatusNotFound, "not_found", "Todo not found")
    51→		return
    52→	}
    53→	RespondJSON(w, r, http.StatusOK, todo)
    54→}
    55→
    56→// Acknowledge marks a TODO as acknowledged. Supports both PATCH (API) and GET with redirect (notification links).
    57→func (h *TodosHandler) Acknowledge(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    58→	id := r.PathValue("id")
    59→	if err := h.store.AcknowledgeTodo(r.Context(), id); err != nil {
    60→		RespondError(w, r, http.StatusNotFound, "not_found", "Todo not found")
    61→		return
    62→	}
    63→
    64→	// If redirect=true, send 302 to the frontend todo page.
    65→	if r.URL.Query().Get("redirect") == "true" && h.publicURL != "" {
    66→		http.Redirect(w, r, h.publicURL+"/todo", http.StatusFound)
    67→		return
    68→	}
    69→
    70→	RespondJSON(w, r, http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"status": "acknowledged"})
    71→}
    72→
    73→// Resolve marks a TODO as resolved. Supports both PATCH (API) and GET with redirect (notification links).
    74→func (h *TodosHandler) Resolve(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    75→	id := r.PathValue("id")
```

All tests pass. Here's a summary of what was implemented:

**Backend (`internal/api/pgstore.go`)**
- Added `aggregated bool` parameter to `ListTodos`
- When `aggregated=true`, uses `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ...)` to keep only the latest todo per source (for release todos, partitions by `source_id`) or per project (for semantic todos, partitions by `project_id`)
- Count query also respects aggregation so pagination totals are correct

**Backend (`internal/api/todos.go`)**
- Updated `TodosStore` interface to include `aggregated bool` parameter
- Handler reads `?aggregated=true` query parameter and passes it through

**Frontend (`web/lib/api/client.ts`)**
- Added `aggregated` parameter to `todos.list()`, sends `aggregated=true` when enabled

**Frontend (`web/app/todo/page.tsx`)**
- Added `aggregated` state toggle
- "Latest only" button in the top-right corner (next to status tabs) toggles the aggregated view
- SWR cache keys include `aggregated` so data refreshes on toggle
- Count badges update to reflect aggregated totals

```
    93→	// Header: "ProjectName vX.Y.Z — 🟢 Low Urgency"
    94→	headerText := title
    95→	if urgency != "" {
    96→		headerText = fmt.Sprintf("%s — %s %s Urgency", title, urgencyEmoji(urgency), urgency)
    97→	}
    98→	// Slack header max is 150 chars
    99→	if len(headerText) > 150 {
   100→		headerText = headerText[:147] + "..."
   101→	}
   102→
   103→	blocks := []any{
   104→		slackBlock{Type: "header", Text: &slackText{Type: "plain_text", Text: headerText}},
   105→	}
   106→
   107→	// Urgency reason (only for Critical/High)
   108→	upperUrgency := strings.ToUpper(strings.TrimSpace(urgency))
   109→	if (upperUrgency == "CRITICAL" || upperUrgency == "HIGH") && urgencyReason != "" {
   110→		blocks = append(blocks, slackBlock{
   111→			Type: "section",
   112→			Text: &slackText{Type: "mrkdwn", Text: fmt.Sprintf("⚠️ %s", urgencyReason)},
   113→		})
   114→	}
   115→
   116→	// Changelog summary
   117→	summary := report.ChangelogSummary
   118→	if summary == "" {

   120→	}

   122→		blocks = append(blocks, slackBlock{
   123→			Type: "section",
   124→			Text: &slackText{Type: "mrkdwn", Text: summary},
   125→		})
   126→	}
   127→
   128→	// First download command only
   129→	if len(report.DownloadCommands) > 0 {

   133→		})
   134→	}
   135→

   140→	}
   141→	if msg.SourceURL != "" {
   142→		footerParts = append(footerParts, fmt.Sprintf("<%s|View on %s>", msg.SourceURL, ProviderLabel(msg.Provider)))
   143→	}
   144→	if msg.ReleaseURL != "" {
   145→		footerParts = append(footerParts, fmt.Sprintf("<%s|View in Changelogue>", msg.ReleaseURL))
   146→	}
   147→	if len(footerParts) > 0 {
   148→		blocks = append(blocks, slackBlock{
   149→			Type: "context",
   150→			Elements: []slackText{
   151→				{Type: "mrkdwn", Text: strings.Join(footerParts, "  |  ")},
   152→			},
   153→		})
   154→	}
   155→
   156→	// Action buttons for TODO acknowledge/resolve
   157→	if msg.TodoID != "" && msg.PublicURL != "" {
   158→		blocks = append(blocks, slackActionsBlock{

   163→			},
   164→		})
   165→	}
   166→
   167→	return blocks
   168→}

   170→func (s *SlackSender) Send(ctx context.Context, ch *models.NotificationChannel, msg Notification) error {
   171→	var cfg slackConfig

   174→	}

   181→	} else {

   183→		// Use attachments for changelog so Slack auto-collapses long text
   184→		// with a "Show more" button.

   187→			changelogText = fields.Changelog
   188→		}

   195→			}

   197→			// Build attachment text: title + version badge, then changelog
   198→			// converted to ASCII and wrapped in a code block. Slack
   199→			// auto-collapses long code blocks in attachments with a

   201→			asciiChangelog := markdownToASCII(changelogText)
   202→			attachText := fmt.Sprintf("*%s* `%s`\n```%s```", msg.Title, msg.Version, asciiChangelog)
   203→
   204→			// Append links after the code block
   205→			var linkParts []string
   206→			if msg.SourceURL != "" {
   207→				linkParts = append(linkParts, fmt.Sprintf("<%s|View on %s>", msg.SourceURL, ProviderLabel(msg.Provider)))
   208→			}
   209→			if msg.ReleaseURL != "" {
   210→				linkParts = append(linkParts, fmt.Sprintf("<%s|View in Changelogue>", msg.ReleaseURL))
   211→			}

   216→				)
   217→			}
   218→			if len(linkParts) > 0 {
   219→				attachText += "\n" + strings.Join(linkParts, "  |  ")
   220→			}
   221→
   222→			attachment := slackAttachment{
   223→				Color:    "#D3D3D3",
   224→				Title:    titleLabel,

   226→				MrkdwnIn: []string{"text"},
   227→			}

   229→				attachment.TitleLink = msg.SourceURL
   230→			}

   232→		} else {
   233→			// No changelog — show a clean version announcement instead of raw JSON.
   234→			headerText := msg.Title

   237→			}

   240→			}

   244→			}

   246→			var linkParts []string
   247→			if msg.Provider != "" && msg.Repository != "" {

   249→			}

   252→			}

   255→			}
```

I see the issue. The test message body is raw changelog JSON (`{"changelog":"## What's Changed\n...","prerelease":"false"}`), not a `SemanticReport`. So Slack's `Send` falls into the **fallback** path (line 181). It parses the body as raw fields and finds a changelog, so it takes the **attachment** path (line 190).

In the attachment path (line 212-217), the acknowledge/resolve links are appended as text links inside the attachment — but Slack attachments can be collapsed and the links might be hidden. However, the real issue is that the test message body **does** have a changelog field, so it goes into the attachment code path which puts the links as inline text, not as proper action buttons.

The action buttons (the `slackActionsBlock`) are only added in the `buildSemanticBlocks` path and the no-changelog fallback path — but **not** in the attachment path because Slack doesn't support mixing attachments with top-level blocks well.

The test message is hitting the attachment path. The links are there but as text inside the attachment, which Slack may collapse. The user likely expects visible buttons. The simplest fix: add an actions block alongside the attachment.

> DEVELOPER

what's if we want to put an acked/resolved version back to pending/acked again, how should we design the user flow?

> AGENT

Good question. Here are a few approaches:

**Option A: Action buttons in each tab**
- On the "Acknowledged" tab, show both a "Resolve" button (move forward) and an "Undo" button (back to Pending)
- On the "Resolved" tab, show a "Reopen" button (back to Pending)
- Simple, discoverable, no extra UI needed

**Option B: Right-click / dropdown menu**
- Replace the single action button with a "..." dropdown menu per row
- Menu items adapt per tab: Pending has "Acknowledge" + "Resolve", Acknowledged has "Resolve" + "Back to Pending", Resolved has "Reopen"
- Cleaner table but adds a click

**Option C: Status dropdown on the row**
- Make the status chip itself a dropdown selector (Pending / Acknowledged / Resolved)
- Any state can transition to any other state
- Most flexible but might feel odd for a linear workflow

**My recommendation: Option A** — it's the simplest, keeps the current pattern, and the use case (undo a mistake) is rare enough that a small secondary button is sufficient. The primary action stays prominent; the undo action is styled more subtly (e.g., ghost/outline style) to signal it's secondary.

The backend already supports arbitrary state changes via `AcknowledgeTodo`/`ResolveTodo`, so we'd just need:
- A new `PATCH /todos/{id}/reopen` endpoint that sets status back to `pending`
- Show the appropriate buttons per tab in the frontend

Want me to go ahead and implement this?

> AGENT

The agent worker is only registered when `NewOrchestrator` succeeds (line 78-84). If it fails (missing `GOOGLE_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY`), the agent worker is skipped with a warning, but the River client is still created without it. Then when you try to trigger an agent run, the job gets inserted but River rejects it because the worker isn't registered.

The fix: skip the River enqueue in `TriggerAgentRun` if the agent worker isn't registered, or better — check before inserting the job.

Actually, the cleaner fix is in `TriggerAgentRun`: it should still insert the `agent_runs` row (for tracking), but only enqueue the River job if the worker is available. Let me check if there's a way to know this.

The simplest approach: catch this specific error and return a clear message to the user.

> AGENT

The River client exists (`s.river != nil`) but the agent worker isn't registered on it, so `Insert` fails with "job kind is not registered". This means the LLM config failed — no `GOOGLE_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set.

This is a configuration issue, not a code bug. You need to set one of these env vars:
- `GOOGLE_API_KEY` — for Gemini (default provider)
- `OPENAI_API_KEY` — for OpenAI (set `LLM_PROVIDER=openai` too)

However, the error message is confusing. Let me improve it to be more user-friendly.

```
    10→// TodosStore defines the data access interface for TODO operations.
    11→type TodosStore interface {
    12→	ListTodos(ctx context.Context, status string, page, perPage int, aggregated bool) ([]models.Todo, int, error)
    13→	GetTodo(ctx context.Context, id string) (*models.Todo, error)
    14→	AcknowledgeTodo(ctx context.Context, id string) error
    15→	ResolveTodo(ctx context.Context, id string) error
    16→	ReopenTodo(ctx context.Context, id string) error
    17→}
    18→
    19→// TodosHandler handles HTTP requests for release TODOs.
    20→type TodosHandler struct {
    21→	store     TodosStore
    22→	publicURL string
    23→}
    24→
    25→// NewTodosHandler creates a new TodosHandler.
    26→func NewTodosHandler(store TodosStore, publicURL string) *TodosHandler {
    27→	return &TodosHandler{store: store, publicURL: publicURL}
    28→}
    29→
    30→// List returns a paginated list of TODOs, optionally filtered by status.
    31→func (h *TodosHandler) List(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    32→	page, perPage := ParsePagination(r)
    33→	status := r.URL.Query().Get("status")
    34→	aggregated := r.URL.Query().Get("aggregated") == "true"
    35→
    36→	todos, total, err := h.store.ListTodos(r.Context(), status, page, perPage, aggregated)
    37→	if err != nil {
    38→		RespondError(w, r, http.StatusInternalServerError, "internal_error", err.Error())
    39→		return
    40→	}
    41→	if todos == nil {
    42→		todos = []models.Todo{}
    43→	}
    44→	RespondList(w, r, http.StatusOK, todos, page, perPage, total)
    45→}
    46→
    47→// Get returns a single TODO by ID.
    48→func (h *TodosHandler) Get(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    49→	id := r.PathValue("id")
    50→	todo, err := h.store.GetTodo(r.Context(), id)
    51→	if err != nil {
    52→		RespondError(w, r, http.StatusNotFound, "not_found", "Todo not found")
    53→		return
    54→	}
    55→	RespondJSON(w, r, http.StatusOK, todo)
    56→}
    57→
    58→// Acknowledge marks a TODO as acknowledged. Supports both PATCH (API) and GET with redirect (notification links).
    59→func (h *TodosHandler) Acknowledge(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    60→	id := r.PathValue("id")
    61→	if err := h.store.AcknowledgeTodo(r.Context(), id); err != nil {
    62→		RespondError(w, r, http.StatusNotFound, "not_found", "Todo not found")
    63→		return
    64→	}
    65→
    66→	// If redirect=true, send 302 to the frontend todo page.
    67→	if r.URL.Query().Get("redirect") == "true" && h.publicURL != "" {
    68→		http.Redirect(w, r, h.publicURL+"/todo", http.StatusFound)
    69→		return
    70→	}
    71→
    72→	RespondJSON(w, r, http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"status": "acknowledged"})
    73→}
    74→
    75→// Resolve marks a TODO as resolved. Supports both PATCH (API) and GET with redirect (notification links).
    76→func (h *TodosHandler) Resolve(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    77→	id := r.PathValue("id")
    78→	if err := h.store.ResolveTodo(r.Context(), id); err != nil {
    79→		RespondError(w, r, http.StatusNotFound, "not_found", "Todo not found")
    80→		return
    81→	}
    82→
    83→	// If redirect=true, send 302 to the frontend todo page.
    84→	if r.URL.Query().Get("redirect") == "true" && h.publicURL != "" {
    85→		http.Redirect(w, r, h.publicURL+"/todo", http.StatusFound)
    86→		return
    87→	}
    88→
    89→	RespondJSON(w, r, http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"status": "resolved"})
    90→}
    91→
    92→// Reopen marks a TODO as pending again, clearing acknowledged/resolved timestamps.
    93→func (h *TodosHandler) Reopen(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    94→	id := r.PathValue("id")
    95→	if err := h.store.ReopenTodo(r.Context(), id); err != nil {
    96→		RespondError(w, r, http.StatusNotFound, "not_found", "Todo not found")
    97→		return
    98→	}
    99→
   100→	RespondJSON(w, r, http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"status": "pending"})
   101→}
```

Now I see the full picture. The Go server runs on port 8080, the Next.js dev server on port 3001. The frontend has no `.env` file and no proxy/rewrite config, so API calls default to `/api/v1` which hits the Next.js server instead of the Go backend.

The fix is to add a Next.js `rewrites` configuration to proxy `/api/v1/*` requests to `http://localhost:8080` during development. This is the standard approach for Next.js dev with a separate backend.

```json
{
  "file_path": "/Users/pc/web3/ReleaseBeacon/web/next.config.ts",
  "content": "import type { NextConfig } from \"next\";\n\nconst isExport = process.env.NODE_ENV === \"production\";\n\nconst nextConfig: NextConfig = {\n  output: isExport ? \"export\" : undefined,\n  ...(!isExport && {\n    async rewrites() {\n      return [\n        {\n          source: \"/api/:path*\",\n          destination: `${process.env.API_BACKEND_URL || \"http://localhost:8080\"}/api/:path*`,\n        },\n      ];\n    },\n  }),\n};\n\nexport default nextConfig;\n"
}
```

The fix is in place. Here's what was wrong:

**Root cause:** The Next.js dev server (port 3001) had no proxy/rewrite configuration. API calls defaulted to `/api/v1` which hit the Next.js server instead of the Go backend (port 8080). GET requests for listing todos may have worked if you had `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` set in your shell or if the Go server was also serving on the same port, but PATCH requests (acknowledge, resolve, reopen) would fail since Next.js doesn't handle those routes.

**Fix:** Added `rewrites` to `next.config.ts` that proxies all `/api/*` requests to `http://localhost:8080` during development. In production (static export), rewrites are excluded since the Go binary serves the frontend directly.

**You'll need to restart the Next.js dev server** (`make frontend-dev` or `cd web && npm run dev`) for the change to take effect. After restart, the acknowledge/resolve/reopen buttons should work.

The error is crystal clear:

> **Access to fetch at 'http://localhost:8080/...' from origin 'http://localhost:3001' has been blocked by CORS policy: Method PATCH is not allowed by Access-Control-Allow-Methods in preflight response.**

Two issues:
1. The request is going directly to `http://localhost:8080` instead of through the Next.js proxy — meaning `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` is baked into the client bundle as `http://localhost:8080`
2. The Go backend's CORS config doesn't allow the `PATCH` method

Found it. Line 70 in `middleware.go`:

```
Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS
```

**`PATCH` is missing** from the allowed methods. The browser sends a preflight `OPTIONS` request for the PATCH, and the server responds without PATCH in the allowed methods, so the browser blocks it.

> AGENT

Good — CORS is applied at the top level in `cmd/server/main.go:140` wrapping the entire mux. So the CORS headers apply to all routes. The only problem was the missing `PATCH` method.

Now you need to restart the Go server for the fix to take effect. Rebuild and restart with `make run` or `make dev`. The acknowledge, resolve, and reopen buttons should then work.

**Summary:** The CORS middleware at `internal/api/middleware.go:70` only allowed `GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS` — `PATCH` was missing. The browser's preflight check for the PATCH requests (acknowledge/resolve/reopen) was being rejected. Added `PATCH` to the allowed methods.

- Source releases link via `releases.source_id` to a source
- Semantic releases link via `semantic_releases.project_id` to a project

```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/pc/web3/ReleaseBeacon/internal/api/pgstore.go",
  "old_string": "func (s *PgStore) AcknowledgeTodo(ctx context.Context, id string) error {\n\ttag, err := s.pool.Exec(ctx,\n\t\t`UPDATE release_todos SET status = 'acknowledged', acknowledged_at = NOW() WHERE id = $1`, id)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"acknowledge todo: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tif tag.RowsAffected() == 0 {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"todo not found\")\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}",
  "new_string": "func (s *PgStore) AcknowledgeTodo(ctx context.Context, id string) error {\n\ttag, err := s.pool.Exec(ctx,\n\t\t`UPDATE release_todos SET status = 'acknowledged', acknowledged_at = NOW() WHERE id = $1`, id)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"acknowledge todo: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tif tag.RowsAffected() == 0 {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"todo not found\")\n\t}\n\n\t// Auto-dismiss (resolve) older pending todos for the same source/project.\n\t// For release todos: resolve other pending todos whose release belongs to the same source\n\t// and was created before this one.\n\t// For semantic todos: resolve other pending todos whose semantic release belongs to the same\n\t// project and was created before this one.\n\t_, _ = s.pool.Exec(ctx, `\n\t\tUPDATE release_todos SET status = 'resolved', resolved_at = NOW()\n\t\tWHERE id != $1 AND status = 'pending'\n\t\tAND (\n\t\t\t-- Same source, older release todo\n\t\t\t(release_id IS NOT NULL AND release_id IN (\n\t\t\t\tSELECT r2.id FROM releases r2\n\t\t\t\tJOIN releases r1 ON r1.source_id = r2.source_id\n\t\t\t\tJOIN release_todos t1 ON t1.release_id = r1.id\n\t\t\t\tWHERE t1.id = $1 AND r2.created_at <= r1.created_at AND r2.id != r1.id\n\t\t\t))\n\t\t\tOR\n\t\t\t-- Same project, older semantic todo\n\t\t\t(semantic_release_id IS NOT NULL AND semantic_release_id IN (\n\t\t\t\tSELECT sr2.id FROM semantic_releases sr2\n\t\t\t\tJOIN semantic_releases sr1 ON sr1.project_id = sr2.project_id\n\t\t\t\tJOIN release_todos t1 ON t1.semantic_release_id = sr1.id\n\t\t\t\tWHERE t1.id = $1 AND sr2.created_at <= sr1.created_at AND sr2.id != sr1.id\n\t\t\t))\n\t\t)`, id)\n\n\treturn nil\n}"
}
```

**Backend:**

**Frontend:**
- `todosApi.acknowledge(id, cascade)` and `todosApi.resolve(id, cascade)` accept optional cascade flag
